title: The Nest Mystery
text: Imagine you are a little bird returning to its nest after a long day of flying. When you reach the nest, you see other birds waiting for you. They share their food, keep you warm, and protect you from the rain. Have you ever wondered why birds live together in nests, and why humans live together in homes?

title: Socratic Question
text: Who are the people waiting for you at home when you return from school? What would happen if everyone lived all alone without anyone to talk to or play with?

content.title: The Tree Analogy
content.description: Think of a tree. A tree has many branches, leaves, and roots, but they are all connected to the same trunk. Just like the branches of a tree, all the people living together in your house are connected to each other!

content.definition: A group of people who are related to each other, care for each other, and usually live together in the same house.

title: Types of Families
text: There are different types of families! A 'Small Family' (or Nuclear Family) has parents and one or two children. A 'Large Family' has parents and more than two children. A 'Joint Family' is a big family where grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts, and cousins all live together happily in one house!

question: What do we call a family where grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts, and cousins live together?

content.title: Are distant relatives family?
content.text: Thinking that family only means people who live in the same house. Sometimes, family members (like grandparents or cousins) live in different cities or even different countries, but they are still a very important part of your family!

title: Reflection time!
text: Think about your own family! How many members are there in your family? Are you in a small family or a joint family? Can you name one special thing you do with your family on Sundays?

title: A Beautiful Connection
text: In ancient Indian traditions, the entire world is considered one big family! This is called 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (The world is one family). Just like your family members help each other, we should help everyone in the world.

content.title: Teacher's Tip for Parents
content.text: Encourage the child to name relations in both English and their mother tongue (e.g., Uncle/Chacha, Aunt/Bua). This builds strong vocabulary and cultural connection.

content.title: Mastery Challenge: The Family Tree
content.text: Draw a beautiful 'Family Tree' on a piece of paper! Write the names of your grandparents at the roots, your parents on the trunk, and you and your brothers/sisters on the branches. Show it to your parents and give them a big hug!
